fullPassage:
Keep Trying and Keep Hoping

People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps.

Seaweed Hamburger Packages

Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.

Your Leather Bags Are Going Un-Leather

What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

questions.passage: Most food packaging is ①<u>coated</u> with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers ②<u>has</u> invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, ③<u>helping</u> prevent food from sticking to paper, while also ④<u>broke</u> down more easily than plastic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: broke → breaking: while also breaking down의 분사구문. helping과 병렬
det.analysis:
✅ ④ broke → breaking: 'while also breaking down' 분사구문. helping과 while also로 병렬
❌ ① coated: is coated with (수동태) 정상
❌ ② has: a team(단수) → has invented 정상
❌ ③ helping: 분사구문 (결과) 정상
det.tip: while also + V-ing: 분사구문 병렬. helping ~ while also breaking ~ 두 분사가 동시 동작

questions.passage: The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands ①<u>planning</u> to choose greener packaging by 2025. Oil-based leathers, ②<u>which</u> make up the majority of artificial leathers, ③<u>requires</u> a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find ④<u>more</u> environmentally friendly options.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: requires → require: 주어 Oil-based leathers(복수) → 동사 require
det.analysis:
✅ ③ requires → require: 주어 leathers(복수). 삽입절(which ~)에 현혹되지 말 것
❌ ① planning: with + 명사 + V-ing 정상
❌ ② which: 계속적 관계대명사, 선행사 leathers 수식 정상
❌ ④ more: 비교급 more environmentally friendly 정상
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: 삽입절(, which ~,)을 건너뛰고 주어(leathers/복수) → 동사(require) 확인

questions.passage: To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been ①<u>proven</u> to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom ②<u>growing</u> from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues ③<u>to grow</u>, more will be invented and ④<u>used</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: growing → grown: 농업 폐기물에서 재배된(grown) 버섯. 수동 과거분사
det.analysis:
✅ ② growing → grown: 'a mushroom grown from farming waste' 버섯이 재배를 '당하는' 것이므로 과거분사(수동)
❌ ① proven: have been proven to V 정상
❌ ③ to grow: continues to V (to부정사) 정상
❌ ④ used: will be invented and used (수동태 병렬) 정상
det.tip: grow: 자동사(자라다) vs 타동사(재배하다). 여기서는 '재배된' 의미 → 수동 과거분사 grown

questions.passage: People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps. Most food ①<u>packaging</u> is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. A team of researchers has invented an ②<u>alternative</u> material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping ③<u>prevent</u> food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more ④<u>difficultly</u> than plastic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 플라스틱보다 더 쉽게(easily) 분해된다. difficultly는 easily(쉽게)의 반의적 표현이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ difficultly → easily: 원문 'breaking down more easily'. 새 소재의 장점이므로 쉽게 분해
❌ ① packaging(포장): 원문 그대로
❌ ② alternative(대안의): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ prevent(방지하다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: easily(쉽게) ↔ difficultly. 새 소재의 장점을 설명하므로 '더 쉽게 분해'가 논리적

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first ①<u>success</u> came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to ②<u>grow</u>, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing ③<u>rapidly</u>. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to ④<u>decline</u> $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장이 2030년까지 12억 달러에 도달(reach)할 것으로 예상된다. decline(감소하다)은 reach(도달하다)와 반대 의미이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ decline(감소하다) → reach(도달하다)가 원문. $725M에서 $1.2B으로 성장하는 맥락에 decline은 모순
❌ ① success(성공): 원문 그대로
❌ ② grow(성장하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ rapidly(빠르게): 원문 그대로
det.tip: reach(도달하다) ↔ decline(감소하다). growing rapidly + valued at $725M → $1.2B은 성장 근거

questions.passage: Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping __________, while also breaking down more easily than plastic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: increase the production of plastic packaging
prevent food from sticking to paper

det.korean: 새 코팅 소재는 음식이 종이에 붙는 것을 방지한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② prevent food from sticking to paper: 원문 기능 서술
❌ ① 플라스틱 포장 생산 증가: 플라스틱 대안 맥락에 반대
❌ ③ 재활용 불가능하게: 친환경 소재 장점과 모순
❌ ④ 모든 천연 용기 대체: 지나친 일반화
det.tip: prevent A from V-ing = A가 ~하는 것을 방지하다. 코팅 소재의 핵심 기능

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As __________, more will be invented and used.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow
oil-based leather production becomes more efficient
the cost of alternative leathers remains too high

det.korean: 친환경 제품에 대한 소비자 수요가 계속 증가하면서 더 많이 발명되고 사용될 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① consumer demand ~ continues to grow: 수요 증가 → 더 많은 발명/사용의 인과관계
❌ ② 석유 기반 가죽 효율: 친환경 대안 논의와 방향 다름
❌ ③ 대안 가죽 비용 높음: '더 많이 사용'과 모순
❌ ④ 환경 규제 완화: 친환경 제품 증가와 모순
det.tip: As A, B: A가 원인, B가 결과. 수요 증가 → 발명/사용 증가

questions.passage: People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps. Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 전 세계 사람들의 환경 보호 노력은 모두 성공했다.
대부분의 식품 포장은 재활용이 매우 쉽다.

det.korean: 연구팀이 해초에서 대안 소재를 발명했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 해초에서 대안 소재 발명: 원문 'invented an alternative material from seaweed' 일치
❌ ① 모두 성공: 'some have succeeded, some have failed' — 일부 실패
❌ ② 재활용 쉽다: 'nearly impossible to recycle' — 거의 불가능
❌ ④ 북호주: 'South Australia' — 남호주
det.tip: 세부 변조 확인: 모두(X) → some, 쉽다(X) → impossible, 북(X) → South

questions.passage: The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic. The material can be made into thin films that can be coated on various surfaces, such as paper or fabric. The fast-food industry is welcoming the news, with major restaurant brands planning to choose greener packaging by 2025.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 새 코팅 소재는 거의 플라스틱처럼 작동한다.
그 소재는 음식이 종이에 붙는 것을 방지한다.
그 소재는 얇은 필름으로 만들 수 있다.

det.korean: 패스트푸드 업계는 이 소식을 환영(welcoming)하고 있다. 부정적이지 않다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 부정적 → welcoming(환영). 긍정적 반응을 부정적으로 변조
❌ ① 원문 'works almost like plastic' 일치
❌ ② 원문 'helping prevent food from sticking to paper' 일치
❌ ③ 원문 'can be made into thin films' 일치
det.tip: welcoming(환영하는) = 긍정적. '부정적'은 반대 변조

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly. In 2022, the market was valued at $725 million and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 석유 기반 가죽은 생산에 적은 에너지가 필요하다.
2030년까지 친환경 가죽 시장은 12억 달러에 이를 것으로 예상된다.
파인애플 잎으로 가죽을 만든 것은 2000년대 첫 성공이었다.
포도 폐기물은 가죽 소재로 전환하는 데 실패했다.

det.korean: 2030년까지 시장이 12억 달러에 이를 것으로 예상된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② $1.2 billion by 2030: 원문 'expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030' 일치
❌ ① 적은 에너지: 'a lot of energy' — 많은 에너지
❌ ③ 2000년대: 'the 1990s' — 1990년대
❌ ④ 실패: 'successfully turned into' — 성공적으로 전환
det.tip: 숫자/연도 세부 확인: $1.2 billion, 1990s, successfully

questions.passage: People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Some have succeeded, some have failed, but remember that every little change helps. Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than plastic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 해초 기반 친환경 포장 소재의 개발

det.korean: 이 글은 해초 기반 친환경 포장 소재 개발에 대한 내용이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 해초 기반 친환경 포장 소재 개발: 핵심 내용 반영
❌ ① 플라스틱 기술 발전: 플라스틱 대안을 다루는 것
❌ ② 해초 양식 경제: 양식이 아닌 포장 소재
❌ ③ 재활용 어려움: 도입부일 뿐, 글의 중심이 아님
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체의 중심 소재. 도입부(문제) vs 본문(해결) 구분

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some have been proven to make alternative leathers. Grape waste from the wine industry and a mushroom grown from farming waste have been successfully turned into leather-like sheets. As consumer demand for eco-friendly products continues to grow, more will be invented and used. The market for eco-friendly leather alternatives is growing rapidly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 석유 기반 가죽은 여전히 가장 효율적인 소재이다.
다양한 친환경 소재가 석유 기반 인조 가죽의 대안으로 개발되고 있다.
파인애플과 포도는 식품 산업에서만 활용 가능하다.

det.korean: 이 글의 요지는 다양한 친환경 소재가 석유 기반 인조 가죽의 대안으로 개발되고 있다는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 친환경 소재 → 석유 기반 가죽 대안: 글 전체의 핵심 주장
❌ ① 효율적: 원문은 문제점(에너지, 분해 시간) 강조
❌ ② 가격/품질: 원문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ 식품 산업만: 가죽 산업에 활용하는 내용
det.tip: 요지 = 글쓴이의 핵심 주장. 문제(석유 기반 가죽) → 해결(친환경 대안) → 전망(시장 성장)

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and <u>the list goes on</u>. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the list goes on이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 가죽 제품의 품질이 계속 향상되고 있다.
가죽으로 만드는 제품의 종류가 매우 다양하다.
가죽 제품의 가격이 계속 오르고 있다.
가죽 산업에서 일하는 사람이 점점 늘고 있다.

det.korean: the list goes on = 목록이 계속된다 → 가죽 제품의 종류가 매우 다양하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 제품 종류가 다양: bags, shoes, clothes, car seats 나열 후 '목록이 계속된다' = 더 많은 종류 존재
❌ ① 품질 향상: 목록 나열과 무관
❌ ③ 가격 상승: 가격 언급 없음
❌ ④ 일하는 사람 증가: 산업 종사자 언급 없음
det.tip: the list goes on = 목록이 계속된다 = 열거한 것 외에도 더 많다. 다양성을 강조하는 표현

questions.passage: People all over the world are making efforts to save the environment. Most food packaging is coated with plastic, making it nearly impossible to recycle. Believe it or not, your hamburger could soon be wrapped in seaweed. A team of researchers has invented an alternative material from seaweed native to South Australia. The new coating material works almost like plastic, helping prevent food from sticking to paper, while also breaking down more easily than <u>it</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 it은 plastic(플라스틱)을 가리킨다. '플라스틱보다 더 쉽게 분해된다'는 비교 대상
det.analysis:
✅ ① plastic: 'breaking down more easily than it(=plastic)' 비교 대상
❌ ② seaweed: 해초 자체가 아닌 플라스틱과 비교
❌ ③ food: 음식이 분해 비교 대상이 아님
❌ ④ paper: 종이가 비교 대상이 아님
det.tip: than + 대명사: 비교 대상. 새 소재 vs plastic의 분해 속도 비교

questions.passage: What is made of leather? Bags, shoes, clothes, car seats, and the list goes on. Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down. So companies have been trying to find more environmentally friendly options. The first success came in the 1990s, when a company made leather from pineapple leaves. To many customers' relief, since then, many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and <u>some</u> have been proven to make alternative leathers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 some이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 some은 eco-friendly ingredients(친환경 재료)를 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ eco-friendly ingredients: 'many other eco-friendly ingredients have been tested, and some(=ingredients) have been proven'
❌ ① companies: 앞 문장의 주어이나 여기서는 ingredients가 선행사
❌ ② customers: 고객은 시험 대상이 아님
❌ ④ alternative leathers: 결과물이지 some의 지칭 대상이 아님
det.tip: some은 바로 앞의 복수명사를 대체. tested → proven 흐름에서 주어는 ingredients

questions.passage: Oil-based leathers, which make up the majority of artificial leathers, require a lot of energy to produce and a long time to break down.
